sections.html:
Danville sits in Southside Virginia on the Dan River, right at the North Carolina border, and is an independent city. It covers about 43 square miles at 531 feet of elevation, roughly 70 miles south of Lynchburg and 45 miles northeast of Greensboro by way of U.S. 29. No county government sits between you and city hall: Danville itself bills the real estate tax, with Pittsylvania County to the north.

The 2020 census counted 42,590 people and the 2025 estimate is 41,647, down from 53,056 in 1990. Slow population loss shapes what sellers see. Fewer buyers compete for some older houses, and the 2020 census found 22,259 housing units with 14.6 percent of them vacant and a rental vacancy rate of 10.7 percent. Price a house with that in mind and expect buyers to compare it with other empty ones on the street.

Tobacco and cotton mills built much of the old housing. Riverside Cotton Mills, founded in 1882 and later known as Dan River Inc., became the largest single-unit textile mill in the world in its day, and the houses put up around that wealth still define whole neighborhoods. When tobacco, textiles and the railroad all restructured late in the twentieth century, the city lost many jobs, and a lot of those houses have gone without steady upkeep since.

Recognized historic districts include the Old West End, Tobacco Warehouse, Downtown Danville, Holbrook-Ross Street and North Main, and the Penn's Bottom stretch of Main Street. Millionaire's Row on Main holds mansions from tobacco planters, and the River District downtown has old warehouses turned into offices, lofts, apartments and restaurants.

  • Find out whether your house is inside a historic district before planning any exterior change.
  • Ask the city whether a tax abatement or relief program applies to your parcel.
  • Collect permits for earlier renovations, since older houses often carry unpermitted work.
  • Expect conventional buyers to balk at foundation, plumbing or wiring problems in a mill-era house.

Manufacturing, healthcare and a newer casino make up the local job mix. Japan Tobacco International, Goodyear, Nestle, Morgan Olson and Sovah Health, Danville are among the larger businesses, and Caesars Virginia opened on December 17, 2024 on the old mill site after voters approved a casino referendum in 2020. Averett University and Danville Community College add education jobs.

Employers here have come and gone. Swedwood, an IKEA subsidiary, opened its first U.S. factory in Danville in 2008 and closed it in December 2019, so some owners sell because a job ended or moved.

sections.h2: Real estate tax rate and due dates
sections.html:
Danville lists its real estate tax at $0.83 per $100 of assessed value. Values and rates run from July 1 through June 30 of the following year, so a new year can bring a new rate.

Billing stepDate or contact
Rate$0.83 per $100 of assessed value
First-half bill mailedBy November 5
First half dueDecember 5
Second-half bill mailedBy May 5
Second half dueJune 5
Real Estate office434-799-5120
Central Collections434-799-5125

The Real Estate office is at 427 Patton Street, Room 301. Have the parcel ID, or the owner's name as it appeared on the July 1 deed, ready when you call. The city also publishes pages on tax relief for elderly or disabled owners, land use and delinquent taxes.

Two money items come up at a Danville closing: whatever city tax is still owed, and the state's grantor tax on the deed. A tax lien jumps ahead of other liens in Virginia and holds until the city is paid, and your contract says who covers which months.

That grantor tax is 50 cents for every $500 of price. The seller bears it unless the contract moves it, and the clerk of court takes payment when the deed is recorded.

Mailing the first-half bill by November 5 and the second by May 5 means a sale in the fall or spring may land between a bill and its due date. Ask your title company to spell out who is covering that installment in the closing statement, so no one is surprised.

  • Get a payoff figure for the current half-year installment before closing day.
  • Ask Central Collections whether any delinquent balance shows on the parcel.
  • Have your title company run a lien and judgment search.
  • Keep any city notices about code violations or utility charges.

Two major U.S. highways meet at Danville, so buyers from Greensboro or Lynchburg can reach it easily. U.S. 58 runs east and west through the main commercial district with a bypass along the Danville Expressway, U.S. 29 runs north and south, and U.S. 360 connects to Richmond. The U.S. 29 bypass is planned as future Interstate 785. Amtrak's Crescent stops at the 1899 station at 677 Craghead Street, and Danville Regional Airport serves general aviation.

Public high schools include George Washington High School and Galileo Magnet High School, along with the Piedmont Governor's School for Mathematics, Science, and Technology. Call the school division for current zoning, because boundaries change.

Local sellers often own something that is old, empty or hard to get a loan on.

  • An inherited house with heirs scattered across other states.
  • A vacant home collecting code notices and vandalism.
  • A mill-era house with deferred maintenance and old wiring.
  • A rental with turnover or rent that never arrived.

Selling for cash means no showings, no repairs and a closing day you pick. Sometimes we buy directly and sometimes a vetted cash buyer steps in; the offer depends on the house's condition and title. Lay it beside a listing before choosing.

It begins with a short talk about the house: how old, what shape, who lives in it, whether taxes are behind. We review photos or stop by, then put an offer on paper. Once you agree, a title company combs the land records for liens, back taxes and anything filed against the owner.

Empty and inherited houses involve extra paperwork. After an owner's death the title company asks who may sign the deed, so pull the estate documents together early. Out-of-state sellers can sign by mail, and a nearby relative can often deliver originals to the title office. Read the settlement statement line by line and ask about anything unfamiliar.

No mortgage means no lender approval to wait for, so the closing date is largely yours within what the title work allows. Before deciding, total what listing would cost: repairs, agent fees and the months of December 5 and June 5 bills, utilities and insurance. Compare that net to the cash figure.

faqs.q: What is the real estate tax rate in Danville, VA?
faqs.a: The city lists $0.83 per $100 of assessed value. Rates take effect July 1 and run through the following June 30, so check the city's Real Estate Taxes page for the current figure.

faqs.q: When are Danville property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax is due December 5 and June 5. The city mails the first-half bill by November 5 and the second-half bill by May 5.

faqs.q: Can I sell a vacant or inherited house in Danville?
faqs.a: Yes. Yes. The heir or executor with legal authority signs the deed, and a cash buyer will take the house as-is. Check that authority with an attorney or the title company first.

faqs.q: Does Virginia charge a transfer tax on the seller?
faqs.a: Virginia imposes a grantor tax of 50 cents per $500 of the sale price on the deed. The seller usually pays it, though the contract can shift some or all of it to the buyer.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Danville real estate tax amounts?
faqs.a: Central Collections answers at 434-799-5125 and the Real Estate office at 434-799-5120. Keep the parcel ID, address or latest bill handy when you phone.
